analysis.title: Homebuilder Confidence Falls in November to Lowest Since Early 2012
key_insights: The seasonally adjusted NAHB Housing Market Index (HMI) fell to 25 in November from 31 in October, the lowest reading since 2012. It came in below the consensus expectation of 29 and well below the 38 recorded in November 2025.
All three HMI components declined in November. The current single-family sales index led the drop, falling six points to 28, its lowest level since late 2011.
Prospective buyer traffic fell from 18 to 16 and expected sales over the next six months fell from 32 to 30. Both remain near 15-year lows and below historical averages and pre-pandemic levels.
Builder confidence fell in all four regions. The Northeast fell six points to 31, the Midwest fell five to 30, the South fell five to 23, and the West slipped to 19 from 20.

Sentiment in the Northeast and Midwest has fallen further below their long-run averages. Confidence in the South and West remains weaker relative to historical norms, reflecting affordability challenges, elevated financing costs and softer demand.

Home prices have kept rising despite high mortgage rates. PNC notes that mortgage rates above roughly 6.5% can intensify the lock-in effect, which keeps existing homeowners from listing and restricts supply.

PNC expects homebuilding activity to remain subdued into 2027. The 30-year fixed mortgage rate is about 7.3%, near its highest in almost three years, and PNC expects it to stay above 7% while US-Iran tensions remain elevated.
Higher energy costs are likely to pressure household budgets and crowd out discretionary spending, while the personal saving rate has trended lower since late 2023.

sector_views.rationale: PNC expects homebuilding activity to remain subdued into 2027, with high mortgage rates, weak buyer traffic and downside risks from energy prices and the Middle East conflict.
